speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng): Mr Speaker, good morning and thank you for prioritising the balance of my Parliamentary Questions (PQs) to be answered this morning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: My response will also cover the matters raised in the two written questions by Mr Christopher de Souza scheduled for 7 February 2024.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Tan See Leng: This builds on my response to retrenchment-related issues at yesterday’s Sitting.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the measures to ensure responsible retrenchment practices and actions that can be taken against recalcitrant employers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This balanced ecosystem ultimately creates more good jobs and sustains them for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And it ensures that even when workers are retrenched, the chances of them finding another good job are high.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is demonstrated by our low long-term unemployment and high labour force participation rates.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: TAMEM also guides unionised companies to notify their unions early about an upcoming retrenchment exercise.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Where it is provided for in the collective agreement, the norm is one month before notifying the employees.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If an employer does not follow the TAMEM, the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) will engage the employer to adhere to the advisory.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Most employers are cooperative when approached by TAFEP or the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This shows that our tripartite advisories are working well without the need for additional penalties, which may negatively affect the wider business environment in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Unionised companies, in particular, have an interest to maintain a good working relationship with their unions as it is a long-term partnership and should not need penalties to do so.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We also work with tripartite partners to assist the affected workers in a timely manner, after we receive the mandatory retrenchment notifications (MRNs).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: MOM has not received any cases of unionised companies who have not submitted MRNs after carrying out a retrenchment exercise.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: More importantly, we continue to help workers upskill, reskill and remain employable.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is so that they can find new and better jobs even when they face disruptions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim raised questions on non-compete clauses and restricted stock units (RSUs).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: To be clear, MOM will not, will never, and does not condone any exploitative employment contracts.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: On non-compete or restraint of trade clauses in employment contracts, the civil courts have clear established principles on when such clauses are acceptable and can be upheld in court; and when such clauses are unreasonable, unjustified and thus, declared void.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The civil courts will assess if there is a genuine business need and whether the company has scoped the clause reasonably based on sector, geographical areas and duration.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The courts will also balance employers’ needs to safeguard their businesses and employees’ ability to earn a living and take into account that the clause should not be used to help businesses gain unfair advantages.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Employees who believe that they are affected by unreasonable or unjustified restraint of trade clauses can seek assistance from their unions, TAFEP or MOM.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We understand that overly restrictive restraint of trade clauses can disadvantage retrenched employees and create difficulties in finding employment.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: On RSUs, under the Employment Act, only non-workmen, which means those who are not mainly involved in manual labour, may be paid salary via stock options such as RSUs.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Such matters are best discussed between the employer and employee as part of their employment contract negotiations.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Employment contracts should clearly indicate the conditions under which unvested RSUs are forfeited.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As these RSUs are typically given to employees in senior positions, they would be able to negotiate the terms with their employers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Hence, MOM does not track the prevalence of RSUs issued.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Employees with disputes over RSUs may file a claim with the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) for mediation, failing which the claim may be referred to the Employment Claims Tribunals for adjudication.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Government will also continue to work closely with tripartite partners to protect workers’ interests and ensure at the same time that Singapore remains a competitive global hub that continues to provide good jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I declare that I have Clementi residents who are affected by the recent Lazada e-commerce retrenchments and that there are sisters and brothers in the Labour Movement who are concerned at the initial reports of what had happened.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have two supplementary questions to the Minister.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: To summarise the first paragraph, the MOM website basically says that for specified companies, notifying MOM of retrenchment exercises will allow the tripartite partners to help affected employees find alternative employment and/or identify relevant training to enhance employability.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Minister, given that in some cases, the retrenchments may be very substantial and involve large numbers of workers, is there a role for mandating earlier notification to MOM when a firm retrenches a very large number of employees, so that help can be provided to the employees early on, in line with the policy objectives on the MOM website?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I understand this was a verbal instruction, but verbal instructions do have weight when a worker is worried about what will happen next.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Minister, does MOM have a position on such non-disclosure arrangements when it pertains to a worker sharing information with a Government agency such as MOM, or for that matter, with a key tripartite partner such as the union?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because some residents have said they are worried.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: When they face such clauses, they are worried about whether they feel comfortable to share with MOM about what has happened or with their Member of Parliament, for that matter.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I want to reassure the hon Member that MOM takes care of all workers, in addition to his Clementi resident.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of TAMEM and TAFEP, we cover every constituency, every division and every Group Representation Constituency (GRC), including from the west to the east, from the south to the north.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That includes residents living in Sengkang and Aljunied GRCs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The important point to note is that the compliance rate over the years has continued to improve.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not have the entire spectrum of statistics, but this five-day MRN period strikes a balance between allowing employers sufficient time to finalise their decisions and collate the required information for submission, while still allowing for the prompt provision of career facilitation services and programmes to assist the affected workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the hon Member, when you run a business, most companies do not want to retrench their employees at will.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For them, retrenchment is always a last resort.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Plans are extremely fluid, and plans can change just before retrenchment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because employers can and would want to adopt other or alternative cost-cutting measures, perhaps the redeployment of affected employees to other roles; hence, we have to strike that very fine balance.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the rest who do not, we continue to work with them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There is TADM, and the unions will continue to represent them, so long as they are unionised.
To the hon Member's resident who was affected, he has also written to me.

So, I hope that that gives you that reassurance that, indeed, in this retrenchment exercise, MOM has been actively, pre-emptively and proactively working behind the scenes with each of our tripartite partners to ensure a swift resolution to this very unfortunate incident.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I wish to take a step back in the process toward the pre-employment aspects of this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I accept that Minister has shared about the plans for stronger regulation in this matter that will be announced in due course.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I could enquire about the possibility of, perhaps, even outright prohibitions on non-competes, but specifically for mid-level and lower-level employees?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While I understand that there are certainly benefits for the inclusion of these kind of clauses, including non-competes for senior roles, my concern has to do with the danger of this kind of inclusion of such boiler-plate language for mid-level and low-level roles because of the chilling effect it can have for employment in general.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Moreover, just like Dr Tan's residents, many of our mid-level and lower-level resident employees cannot afford legal recourse, unlike senior employees.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, we do not have intention to introduce more regulations.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, let us be clear on that part of it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have, prior to this incident, planned quite extensively and worked on various initiatives with our tripartite partners to come up with guidelines on such clauses.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And as I have said, it so happened that the Lazada retrenchment happened at this time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Having said that, it would not be possible for us to regulate every single negotiated contract because the nature of businesses, from financial services, fintech to manufacturing, to all kinds of professional services and so on – if there is a one-size-fits-all solution, I would really like to hear how that could ever be possible.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we have undertaken is a nuanced approach where any senior-level employee, in terms of the negotiation, can always reach out to TADM and if it exceeds beyond certain claim limits, there is also the civil courts for them to take action.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Assoc Prof Lim was saying that this group of mid-level employees may not have the ability to do so.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Generally, we will help them but in the negotiation of RSUs, stock options, in lieu of actual wages and so on, I think most of them are at a different level of seniority, maturity and experience when they negotiate and enter into such contracts.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that we should not think of smearing across as a one-size-fits-all policy because I think that would be setting ourselves back.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And if I could clarify to the Member Mr Murali that, that is precisely because why I mentioned the dangers of these boiler-plate language – because of the chilling effect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Even if they are unenforceable in a court of law, the danger is that they have a negative effect on employee rights, even before they can be potentially challenged.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have a short supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister share whether MOM has any of these early warning or intelligence capabilities that can ascertain which unionised companies intend to carry out retrenchment exercises, so that the tripartite partners can do some preparatory or advance work to help workers that are about to be retrenched?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think, in an ideal world, we would like to have information available to us at our fingertips all the time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But, as I have shared earlier on, retrenchments typically are one of the last resort measures that a company would resort to.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, having said that, there are other proxy indicators, for instance, like market disruptions, geopolitical uncertainties, disruptions in terms of transformation, new technology – these are things that we face as an open economy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, our preventive, pre-emptive and very proactive stance has always been to make sure that all of our workers continue to be equipped to have that resilience to withstand all of these disruptions by upskilling and reskilling.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And we do not just support the workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have indeed rolled out significant number of measures to support our businesses as well to help them transform.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, you have the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), pari passu with that with the Job Transformation Maps, we have rolled out Career Conversion Programmes to help businesses and employees with conversions in terms of their careers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And we also work very closely with our Labour Movement, our brothers and sisters, in rolling out Company Training Committees, which is spearheaded by the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And there are e2i and Workforce Singapore (WSG) to help these workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We believe that a very comprehensive holistic solution is much better than trying to understand and pick out which one particular company is going to have retrenchments and and try to stop it.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will just say that there are employers, and there are employers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think I we are only at Question No 3.
